metadata.name: Hindu nationalism
metadata.description: An Indian nationalist tradition that places Hindu civilisation at the centre of national identity. Its contemporary BJP/RSS strand combines cultural integration, national sovereignty and social traditions with elections, economic development, domestic enterprise and targeted welfare.
metadata.period: Contemporary Indian tradition, 2014–2025; foundational context from 1965
metadata.scope: The contemporary Indian Hindu nationalist tradition associated with the BJP and RSS, assessed through its programmes and statements of doctrine rather than treating Narendra Modi or one government as the entire ideology. Internal economic and institutional differences are retained. Evidence checked on 5 October 2026; this is not a claim to document every development after the latest cited 2025 statement.
metadata.phrase: Society should be united around India’s Hindu civilisational heritage, preserve its traditions and sovereignty, and pursue development that strengthens national self-reliance and provides for those in need.

axes.brief: Elections and parliamentary institutions are part of the contemporary programme. Assess constitutional restraints separately from a preference for decisive national leadership.
axes.counterEvidence: Foundational criticism of concentrated power supports institutional limits; scholarship also describes majoritarian pressures. Neither electoral success nor criticism establishes endorsement of every check or unilateral rule. IDE researcher Hiroshi Sato describes leadership authority and community duties taking precedence over rights; this challenges the more constitutional interpretation of doctrine and is retained as counter-evidence rather than treated as a questionnaire submission.
